text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
RZECZPOSPOLITA

- Striking miners at the Belchatow brown coal mine have stopped coal deliveries to the Belchatow power station and demanded the dismissal of the mine's director whom they accuse of mismanagement, said Czeslaw Maconko, a strike leader.
- Poland's record firms sold around 28.5 million records and cassettes last year worth 338.4 million zlotys, a recent report by the Audio-Video Producers' Association said.
- The Polska Zegluga Morska (PZM) shipping firm made a net loss of 25 million zlotys last year, a significant change compared with the 30 million zlotys net profit the year before.

- The increased price of the green card insurance policy for drivers abroad may threaten Polish-German cooperation development in border areas, representatives of the Pomerania Euroregion grouping over 50 communes in Poland's Szczecin province and Germany's Brandenburg amd Meklemburg said.

- Stocznia Gdynia shipyard launched a 30,600 deadweight tonne (DWT) container ship, the Westermes, contracted by a German shipowner. The shipyard will construct 31 vessels worth $1.2 billion by the second half of 1999, the yard said.
- The Amica household durable maker will employ 50 disabled people in a new computerised refrigerator component plant in Ostrowiec Swietokrzyski, southern Poland.

- Over 15 percent of Poland's labour force works in the so-called grey zone, meaning they do not pay taxes. This is estimated to deprive the country of between 10 to 20 percent of tax revenues, the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said.
- Poland's forests will increase by 700,000 hectares by 2020 and grow further by 1.2 million hectares before the end of 2050, the forestry research institute official Bohdan Lakiewicz said.
NOWA EUROPA
- Over 500,000 Poles have access to Internet's World Wide Web and the growth in the number of web-surfers is Europe's highest, NASK academic computer network official Maria Baranowska said.

- Former finance and foreign minister Andrzej Olechowski has been appointed a mediator in the Gdansk refinery dispute between the employees and management. The workers want a 15 percent share stake in the plant when it is privatised.
- Poland's limousine car dealers sold 1,500 vehicles in 1996. Sweden's Volvo sold 553 limousines, which gave it the biggest market share, the Samar monitoring agency said.
- The investments of U.S.-based firms in Poland increased by 40 percent last year compared with 1995, totalling up to $4 billion, U.S. Ambassador to Poland Nicholas Rey said.

- Poland's exports were $24.346 billion last year, which showed a $1.45 billion growth compared with 1995, while imports reached $36.9 billion and exceeded 1995 results by $7.8 billion, the economy ministry's economic analysis department said.
- In the next few weeks the Bumar Labedy heavy industry and arms plant will sign a contract with Poland's defence ministry for this year's deliveries of armoured tanks.
GAZETA WYBORCZA

- The BZ Lubusz breweries have demanded that the listed Okocim breweries should discontinue production of the Okocim Zagloba beer and pay it three million zlotys in damages. The "Zagloba" trademark was reserved by Lubusz six months before Okocim applied for it, BZ Lubusz president Dariusz Wolak said.
- Lublin municipality plans a new bond issue to buy 100 new buses for the urban transport services in the next few years, Lublin president Pawel Brylowski said.
ZYCIE
- JTT Computer hardware maker and distributor sold 37,000 personal computers last year, which gave it a 10 percent market share and placed it second only to the listed Optimus computer firm.
